newsitem.title: UK: BAA shares slip, traders say profit taking.
newsitem.headline: BAA shares slip, traders say profit taking.

text.p: Shares in airport operator BAA Plc dropped on Friday, with traders putting the 19.5 pence fall down to a combination of profit-taking and general market nervousness.
BAA shares were quoted at 577.5 pence by 1115 GMT. They reached a peak of 607 pence earlier this month.
"All I can think is they have had a good run lately," said one trader, adding some players may have decided to take profits. But volume was moderate with around 1.5 million shares traded.
Suggestions that one market-maker had been "aggressively moving around" the stock was denied by the firm in question. "It's nothing to do with us," a trader there said.
Others said the strength of sterling could have an impact on spending by passengers travelling through London's Heathrow and Gatwick airports, but none had heard of any profit downgrades.
One said the strike at British Airways Plc two weeks ago was not seen as a major factor.

BAA shares have risen sharply since the UK's July 2 budget on relief that its liability to the Labour government's "windfall tax" on privatised utilities was less than feared, at an estimated 70-100 million stg, payable over two years.
BAA's first quarter results are scheduled for release on Tuesday, August 5.
